dependencies.label: Community Relations & Social License
dependencies.description: Dependency on maintaining community trust and acceptance for continued operational legitimacy. Particularly material where operations have significant local footprint or where projects require ongoing community consent.
indicators: FPIC (Free, Prior, Informed Consent) policies in place (Y/N)
sources: SASB Community Relations topic (EM-EP-210a, IF-EU-210a, IF-HB-210a)
ESRS S3 Affected Communities — Paragraphs 8–16 (social licence, engagement)
IFC Performance Standard 1 (2012) — Stakeholder Engagement
FPIC — ILO Convention 169 (Indigenous and Tribal Peoples Convention)
UN Guiding Principles on Business & Human Rights 2011 — Pillar 3 (Remedy)

dependencies.label: Indigenous Peoples & Human Rights
dependencies.description: Obligation to respect indigenous peoples' rights and broader human rights in operations and supply chains. Failure creates legal, reputational, and operational risk particularly in extractives, forestry, and infrastructure.
indicators: FPIC processes documented for all relevant projects
Human rights due diligence assessment conducted (Y/N)
Number of human rights incidents in supply chain
% of operations with community benefit agreements
sources: UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP) 2007
IFC Performance Standard 7 (2012) — Indigenous Peoples
UN Guiding Principles on Business & Human Rights 2011 — Human Rights Due Diligence
ESRS S3 Affected Communities — specific provisions on indigenous peoples
OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises 2023 — Chapter IV (Human Rights)

dependencies.label: Customer Data Privacy & Cybersecurity
dependencies.description: Dependency on customer trust through secure handling of personal and sensitive data. Breaches lead to regulatory fines (GDPR), litigation, and reputational damage. Universally material but especially acute for data-intensive businesses.
indicators: % of employees trained on data privacy annually
sources: UK GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) / Data Protection Act 2018
ESRS S4 Consumers and End-users — Paragraphs 9–12 (privacy, data security)
SASB Customer Privacy topic (FN-CB-230a, TC-SI-230a, HC-BP-230a)
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 — Information Security Management Systems
ICO (Information Commissioner's Office) — Data Protection Accountability Framework

dependencies.label: Access to Products & Services
dependencies.description: Dependency on maintaining broad, equitable access to essential products and services. Particularly relevant for financial services (financial inclusion), utilities (essential services), and healthcare. Regulatory and social expectations around affordability are growing.
indicators: % of customers in vulnerable or low-income segments
Affordability measures / hardship schemes in place
Complaints related to access or affordability
sources: ESRS S4 Consumers and End-users — Paragraphs 13–16 (access & affordability)
SASB Access & Affordability topic (FN-CB-240a, HC-BP-240a, IF-WU-240a)
FCA Consumer Duty 2023 — four consumer outcomes framework
UN SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) — equal access to financial services
UK Equality Act 2010 — Duty to make reasonable adjustments

dependencies.label: Product Safety, Quality & Liability
dependencies.description: Dependency on delivering safe, high-quality products that meet regulatory standards. Product recalls, safety incidents, or quality failures generate financial, legal, and reputational risk.
indicators: Regulatory warnings or fines for product safety
sources: SASB Product Quality & Safety topic (HC-BP-250a, FB-AG-250a, TR-AU-250a)
ESRS S4 Consumers and End-users — product safety disclosures
UK Consumer Rights Act 2015 — satisfactory quality, fitness for purpose
GRI 416: Customer Health and Safety 2016
EU General Product Safety Regulation 2023 (GPSR)

dependencies.label: Responsible Selling Practices & Marketing
dependencies.description: Risk of mis-selling, predatory pricing, or deceptive marketing practices that harm customers. Relevant to financial products, consumer goods, and media. Growing regulatory scrutiny (FCA, ASA, Digital Markets Act).
indicators: % of products with accurate sustainability claims
sources: SASB Selling Practices & Product Labeling topic (FN-CB-270a, FB-TB-270a)
ESRS S4 Consumers and End-users — marketing and labelling practices
FCA Principles for Business — Principle 6 (Customers' Interests)
ASA UK Advertising Codes — misleading advertising rules
EU Green Claims Directive (proposed 2023) — substantiation requirements

dependencies.label: Supply Chain Labor Standards & Modern Slavery
dependencies.description: Exposure to forced labour, child labour, unsafe working conditions, and wage theft in supply chains. UK Modern Slavery Act obligations apply to large LSE companies. Growing due diligence expectations under proposed UK legislation.
indicators: % of suppliers audited on labour standards
Number of supplier non-conformances on labour standards
% of Tier 1 suppliers with living wage compliance
sources: UK Modern Slavery Act 2015 — §54 Transparency in Supply Chains
ESRS S2 Workers in the Value Chain — Paragraphs 9–17 (due diligence, wages)
ILO Core Labour Standards — Conventions 29, 87, 98, 105, 111, 138, 182
UN Guiding Principles on Business & Human Rights 2011 — HRDD in supply chains
OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Responsible Business Conduct 2018

dependencies.label: Supply Chain Resilience & Diversity
dependencies.description: Concentration risk in supply chains — single-source dependencies, geographic concentration, and supplier financial health. Supply disruptions create operational and financial risk, as highlighted by pandemic and geopolitical events.
indicators: % of suppliers with business continuity plans
sources: ESRS S2 Workers in the Value Chain — supply chain mapping requirements
SASB Supply Chain Management topic (TC-HW-430a, FB-AG-430a)
ISO 28000:2022 — Security and Resilience — Supply Chain Security Management
UK National Risk Register 2023 — supply chain concentration risks
World Bank Enterprise Surveys — supply chain diversification indicators

dependencies.label: Regulatory Compliance & Relationships
dependencies.description: Dependency on maintaining a constructive relationship with regulators and ongoing compliance with laws and regulations. Fines, licence revocations, or adversarial regulatory relationships create direct cost and operational risk.
sources: ESRS G1 Business Conduct — Paragraphs 7–14 (corporate culture, anti-bribery)
SASB Business Ethics topic (FN-CB-510a, EM-EP-510a)
UK Bribery Act 2010 — Section 7 (failure to prevent bribery)
GRI 205: Anti-corruption 2016 (GRI 205-1 Operations assessed for corruption risk)
OECD Anti-Bribery Convention 1997 — enforced via UK Serious Fraud Office

dependencies.label: Anti-competitive Behaviour & Market Integrity
dependencies.description: Risk of anti-competitive practices including price-fixing, market allocation, and abuse of dominant position. CMA and EU competition enforcement creates significant financial exposure.
sources: Competition Act 1998 (UK) — Chapter I & II prohibitions
TFEU Articles 101–102 — EU competition law (cartel conduct, abuse of dominance)
ESRS G1 Business Conduct — anti-competitive behaviour disclosures
GRI 206: Anti-competitive Behaviour 2016
CMA (Competition and Markets Authority) — UK enforcement priorities 2024

dependencies.label: Local Economic Impact & Value Distribution
dependencies.description: Dependency on being perceived as a positive contributor to local and national economies. Companies that extract value without sharing it locally face growing political and reputational risk including windfall taxes and operating restrictions.
indicators: Community investment (£ and % of pre-tax profit)
sources: ESRS S3 Affected Communities — Paragraphs 17–22 (local economic contribution)
GRI 203: Indirect Economic Impacts 2016 (GRI 203-1 Infrastructure & services)
SASB Community Relations topic — local economic development metrics
ISO 26000:2010 — §6.8 Community Involvement and Development
UN SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) — local job creation

dependencies.label: Systemic Financial Risk & Stability
dependencies.description: For large financial institutions, dependency on maintaining systemic stability and public trust in the financial system. Counterparty risk, leverage, and exposure to distressed assets create systemic contagion risk.
indicators: Climate & nature-related financial risk stress test results
sources: Basel III Framework (BIS 2017) — systemic risk capital requirements
Bank of England Financial Stability Reports — systemic institution monitoring
ESRS G1 Business Conduct — systemic risk governance
UK Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 — systemic risk provisions
FSB (Financial Stability Board) — SIFI designation framework

dependencies.label: Financing the Transition & Sustainable Products
dependencies.description: For financial institutions, the dependency on developing credible transition finance and sustainable investment products to maintain competitiveness, regulatory compliance, and investor confidence.
indicators: % of investment portfolio aligned with net zero
ESG product AUM as % of total AUM
sources: EU Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR) 2021 — Article 8 & 9 products
EU Taxonomy Regulation 2020 — substantial contribution to climate mitigation
ESRS E1 Climate Change — transition finance exposure metrics
SASB Environmental Risk Exposure topic (FN-CB-410a, FN-IB-410a)
NGFS Scenarios for Central Banks and Supervisors 2022
